title: Portal registry
description:
Every portal game the Factory knows for one title: one file per title, one entry per platform. It exists so that no publish visit ever creates a second game for a title on a portal, and so that a game a person created by hand in a portal's console can be linked to the title instead of duplicated.

Like `state`, this is a mutable cursor and carries no provenance: it is rewritten whenever a portal game is created, found, associated or observed, and pinning it by hash would make every observation invalidate every reference to it. What makes it auditable is each entry's `history[]`, append-only, one item per recorded change, saying who made it (automation or a person), in which run, and why.

A status that only a portal can establish - `PENDING_REVIEW`, `VERIFIED`, `PUBLISHED`, `REJECTED` - is recorded only with evidence of the portal's own status text, never inferred from a click that returned. Changing the portal game id of an existing entry is a person's act. Entries are independent: a rejection on one platform leaves every other platform's entry as it was.

x-wgf.note: Written by scripts/wgf_publish/registry.py, which refuses a transition the module's table does not allow, a portal-established status without evidence, and an automated change of a recorded game id. A person links a game with `wgf-publish.py registry associate`.

portals.description: Platform id (a platform profile id) to the portal game known there. A platform with no entry is NOT_CREATED: no game is known for this title on it.

portal.description: The portal's own name for itself, as its console shows it.

game_title.description: The game's title as entered on the portal.

external_game_id.description: The portal's id for the game, read back from the portal or linked by a person. The first id the find-game phase tries. Changed only by a person.

app_id.description: A second portal id where the portal has one (an app id distinct from the game id).

other_ids.description: Any further portal identifiers, by the portal's own name for them.

url.description: The game's page or console URL on the portal.

submission_status.description: The portal's own wording for the last submission's state, verbatim.

publication_status.description: The portal's own wording for the game's publication state, verbatim.

build_hash.description: The build last uploaded to this game. A different build makes every submission fact recorded for the old one stale.

campaign_hash.description: The store listing (copy and media) last applied to this game.

association.description: How this game came to be known: the Factory created it and read its id back; a person linked a game they created; or the Factory found it on the portal (a recorded or configured id that resolved).

last_checked_at.description: When the portal's state was last read.

evidence.description: What the recorded statuses rest on: the portal's status text, a screenshot, an API response. Hashed; the content lives where `ref` says, redacted.

history.description: Append-only, oldest first: one item per recorded change to this entry.
